source_doc: This continues to be very popular!  Three dogs, and they love it. I was dubious about how this would hold up, or that it would keep my dog's interest, but after three months it is still a hit!  I mean, I know it's the FOOD that makes them interested, but they all will keep moving around, finding every last piece of dog food out of it.  It takes some time to load, but I've found that I can just sprinkle regular dog food (small bite sized) while I'm spreading apart the folds and it goes pretty quickly.  I expected that with two puppies and an adult dog that they'd start chewing up the polar-fleece type fabric, but they haven't done that at all.  It's big enough that it doesn't slide around, since they're typically standing on at least part of it, and I like that I can just fold it and then roll it up, with the built-in strap holding it together like a small sleeping bag.  When I want to use it, I just unroll, load the kibble in, and then I let the dogs in from outside and watch them just go at it!  They're busy, busy, busy, with their tails wagging the whole time.  I love it!

source_doc: Not a fan. I liked this keyboard at first.  I work from home and although my employer happily provides me with a keyboard that functions just fine.  I don't like cords.  My old Logitech wireless keyboard was still going strong but I wanted something you could actually see letters on the keys on, I'd worn the writing off of most of my keys.  So I picked this one, I didn't notice that it was rechargeable until after it arrived.  I thought oh that's kind of cool no more batteries.  Then about day four middle of a phone call with a client my keyboard just stops working.  I tried quickly plugging it in to my phone charger hoping it would allow me to keep typing, but no it didn't. There was no warning that it was about to run out battery life 🔋, no battery power warning or anything.  I tried it again after being plugged in for a while and it worked again.  However I can't have my keyboard just stop working mid work day.  So I returned it for something without flashing keys and something that ran off batteries.  In the 5 years my Logitech was in use I only put a new battery in it once.  If you can remember to charge it daily it might be great.

source_doc: Comparable to other standard wipers but is definitely not premium. I was fortunate in the fact that I got to utilize the wipers in the rain and slush right away on a 10 hour drive across state (California 2/24/2023) and it happened to rain 9 out of those 10 hours too. On a side note, I did buy three sets for all my cars and none of them came labeled with the sizing so I had to measure the lengths to determine which was for which vehicle.

source_doc: Very easy to use. I bought this for my front door because I noticed light and cold air leaking through where the door meets the frame.  I must admit that I am not very handy and a bit of a diy dunce.  I really thought this would be a good temporary fix until I could call a handyman. Simply measure out how much you need and cut it to size.  Clean off the area first.  I used rubbing alcohol because it dries so quickly.  This helps the adhesive stick to the surface without getting messed up by dirt or dust.  Peel off the backing and stick it in place with a fair amount of pressure.  I let it cure for 24 hours before I used the door again.  That might be excessive,  but I wanted to be extra cautious.  The D shape is really neat because it expands into the little gaps.  Nothing is getting through now.

source_doc: Great replacement and easy to install - All tools were included. I've had my Aeron chair for nearly ten years. I picked it up used to replace my crappy old chair from one of the big box stores when it finally gave up the ghost. So recently I heard a "crack" and saw that the back frame of the seat had finally worn down and broken.I was beside myself. I didn't want to buy another chair, so I looked for repair shops in the area. One of the shops referred me direct to this product page and said, "order this, and if you want, I can install it." So I did.Fast forward and, still sitting on the broken seat, busy with work, I decided to look up what the repair entailed. I found a tutorial on youtube. Four bolts for the seat. Two nuts to transfer the j-bars. I figured I could handle it.This replacement seat kit came with the hex wrench needed to undo the seat, and a fitted wrench and a T25 torx driver to quickly transfer the j-bar. It took a few minutes, and a bit of leaning in because the bolts were really in there, but the replacement was easy. I literally didn't take out my toolbox because I had everything I needed in the kit.Really well designed chair and replacement was super easy. Five stars.

source_doc: I love this brand. So i actually bought the white one last year and i loved it but the keys where so loud but overall i loved it. I am a gamer, and the mouse did start to miss a few clicks so i decided it was time for a new keyboard and mouse. I decided to go with the pink one this time because white is hard to keep clean and i just didnt want to do the black since my mouse pad and mic are black. Anyways i actually love the pink one a lot more and the keys are a lot quitter, and the lights are more fun and easier to control and there are so many more options with this one then the one i had before. The only issue that i have is the space bar is a little harder to hit. And while that isn't a big deal for just typing it can be when you miss a jump in a game. Other than that, yeah i would buy this keyboard and mouse again. the mouse is perfect so far and I haven't missed a click.

source_doc: Exactly what I needed. These are great! I started woodworking and whittling as a hobby and the gloves are the best. I recently burnt my thumb while cooking and was still worried I'd stab my thumb while working. Sure if I intentionally tried to make the knife go into the glove it will happen, it's cut resistant not stab resistant. I have accidentally stabbed a few fingers but there was enough padding for it to cushion it so I didn't bleed or get seriously hurt. I mainly use whittling knives, though.The bumpy grip stuff is great. I have arthritis in my hands and sometimes things slip my grasp, but not with these.Make sure to order a size down because like the other reviewers say: they run big. I would fit a medium by the charts standards but I fit into a small. I have no problem with the finger length since I have "piano player length" fingers. Your hands will get sweaty if worn too long but isn't super horrible, I wear them for 3-5 hrs at a time.They don't wear down too fast. With what I do and judging by the one month I've had them, I could see them lasting 3-4 months before needing to replace them.I give all 5 stars cause it's exactly what I was looking for.

source_doc: The seam is so close to the curved edges at the bottom that it could eventually rip. I have a 30 oz. insulated water bottle that I strive to fill 3X with water to drink throughout the day.  I take it with me when I drive, positioning it in the cup holder.  However, there are times when I walk that I wish I could take my water bottle with me.  I ordered this 2 pack of Tainehs Water Bottle Holders because I figured my bottle would fit inside it based upon the product page's measurements: 7.4" X 3.5", and my boyfriend could use the other bottle holder when we go hiking.  I like the rectangular shape to fit keys, a Chapstick, a protein bar, etc.  I could slide a credit card, money, ID, etc. in the front zipper pocket, in case we stop somewhere to walk and shop.I think these water bottle carriers are handy. The nylon material feels durable. The inch-wide strap is adjustable.  My only concern is the stitching.  The seam is so close to the curved edges at the bottom of the black one that it could eventually rip and come apart at some point.  The pink one isn't as bad.  (See photos.) The current price of $16 might be a bit high, IMO, but you do get 2 of them.

source_doc: I bought this for my two dogs excessive itching. -This was nicely packaged.  No breaks or leaks.  Also came with three different pumps.  A screw on/off, pop top, and a pump. source_doc: Awesome keyboard for those that loved the IBM Model M. I have been looking for a new keyboard for a while. I have been using a Logitech model that supported 3 computers. It was OK, but the keys were very mushy. I downsized to one computer so I thought why not switch to a new keyboard too. I knew I wanted something similar to my old beloved IBM Model M keyboard, but something without the large size and also had wireless capabilities. After MUCH searching for a decent mechanical keyboard, I focused on the Royal Kludge models. Mostly for the excellent price, as some mechanical keyboards can be costly. I got the 90% model, and I couldn't be happier. The feel is very similar to the Model M, but definitely quieter (although not exactly silent.) What I love most besides the feel is the magnetically attached wrist rest. That feature alone is pretty neat. There are plenty of other options I have yet to explore of fully utilize, such as the lighting of the keyboard. I have yet to play with many of the key mappings either. But I mostly just type, so these features aren't very important to me. Note: I am running Linux (Pop! OS to be specific), and the keyboard works great with Linux out of the box.

source_doc: Not just a pregnancy pillow! I had 2 major abdominal surgeries and was absolutely struggling to find a comfortable way to sleep. When sleeping on my non surgical side, I rolled to my belly in my sleep waking me up in terrible pain. I gave this pillow a go. I wish I’d have gotten one of these years ago! It comes vacuum packed, I tossed it in the dryer on air fluff for about 30 mins and left it out to form as suggested and washed the cover in my sensitive detergent (dried cover on very low heat because of the fabric type). It formed beautifully! I couldn’t wait to try it out. I did add a bit of extra poly fill on one side to make it more firm only because I wanted a firm barrier to prevent me from rolling on my belly. It worked perfectly! I never rolled on to my belly once. I’ve been using this all week now and I have noticed that my incision sites aren’t anywhere near as painful and it’s even helped with painful joints from fibromyalgia. I wish I could give it far more stars. It wasn’t flat like many other pillows and their reviews, it was truly perfect. This is a fantastic investment. Now I just have to work on getting the hubby to stop resenting my pillow for replacing him lol

source_doc: Super soft exactly what I was looking for. I bought this bc I have a hole in one of the cushions of my couch and I just don't have the money to buy a new couch. Anyway. This cover is really nice. It feels super soft like a brand new couch and super stretchy. I got a large for my couch and I think I could've used an extra large since my cushions are very big. I'm 8 months pregnant and i got it on by myself in maybe 10 minutes after I figured out how it was supposed to go. It's mostly walking circles around your couch pulling on it until it doesn't look weird. I also obviously didn't care too much about that, it covered a hole. I got black because it was the cheapest, if you don't like obvious pet hair or dirt marks, obviously black is a bad choice for you, be aware of that. Overall it's super nice and I'll probably buy more to keep rotating until I can buy a new one but I'm super happy with this. I haven't tried the water resistant factor but even if it's not, I'm not mad about it.

source_doc: Maiden voyage success. I was looking for an affordable sleep system that didn't frustrate me like the perpetual tangled mess I was in my mummy bag but that would still be cozy and warm. I'm a toss-n-turn sleeper from side to tummy to side and mummy bags are too tight around the legs and don't let you roll over. I tried this for the first time tent camping at Valley of Fire in late December and it worked out great. Temps were in the mid-'30s to low '40s and I was plenty warm with this and my r4 sleeping pad. I did pull it up over my head for added warmth during the night when it got windy. (I'm 5'7", 155 lbs) It has slick fabric on both sides so that was the only minor drawback. It slipped off my body when I rolled over but I was wearing silky long johns so I will revisit my sleep clothes for future trips. I swapped the compression sack it came with for one that has four straps and was able to decrease the packable size. I didn't wear it as a poncho this trip but I'm heading to the Grand Canyon in late Feb so I may use it to hang around camp.

I wish i knew about this last year when i went to busch gardens, i may have enjoyed the rides more but now that i have it ill be good for next time.

source_doc: Learning How To Play at 66! I have loved Gospel Music since I was 18 years old!  I vowed that I would learn to play it at some point in my life. Well that point is here and after looking for the standard organ in Black churches, I decided that I didn’t need a Hammond and Leslie in our house.  After researching dozens of keyboards and reading hundreds of reviews, boom!  Here I am with this keyboard in my house and me practicing scales with proper finger placement!  This is an amazing keyboard. It is amazing how accurate the instruments are and it has organ voices that emulate the Hammond and Leslie, which is the main reason I bought it!  I am so excited about the feel of the keys and the ability for it to run off of AA batteries!!Now that I have no excuse, it is on to the included DVD and booklet and YouTube instructional videos for playing Black Gospel music and finally my next purchase of full size base pedals that plug into it. Yes, I have a headset so that my wife doesn’t need to endure what we endured when our kids were learning instruments. I highly recommend this amazing instrument. Top quality and design and a definite value for the money.

source_doc: Disappointment. Bought these based on the reviews that were like "Oh my god these damaged my stairs when I removed them!" because I didn't plan on removing them and I wanted them to stick as good as possible.Well... they don't. These are old stairs. Still though, I prepped them as I would anything that I plan to stick with adhesive. They were very easy to stick down but unfortunately they're not that sticky. I've walked over each piece on each stair back and forth multiple times to get as much pressure on every point of contact and they just won't stay stuck. I don't know what to do other than maybe some contact cement around all the edges.These are cheap and look alright. I'd be more upset if they were priced higher but I should have figured this would be the outcome for what I paid. I guess I was just hoping that the reason other reviews say they damage stairs when they're removed is because they stick SO well. Not the case, actually.

source_doc: Didn’t Work. I bought one of these quite a while ago and never installed it. I finally got around to installing it. The concept is great, mine just didn’t work. I tried it on two different Leviton switches thinking that perhaps the contacts just didn’t quite line up on the first switch I tried to install it on. I made sure the switch (on the SnapPower faceplate) was in, power was in to the switch, and I covered the sensor/switch to test it. Nothing. I removed the SnapPower faceplate, inspected it, and tried again. Same result. I tried another switch, and same result. I had an extra Leviton switch, so I checked to see whether the SnapPower contacts line up with the screws. They do, not perfectly, but certainly enough to make adequate electrical contact that they should work. So either my SnapPower face plate is defective, or it doesn’t work if the hot and return wires are connected to the switch using the push-in connectors rather than the connector screws? It has been too long for me to return this one, so I’m stuck with an overly expensive spare faceplate. I’m pretty handy and technically savvy, and these are ultra simple, so it’s definitely an issue with the one I bought.

I did not have this shampoo,  so I did a quick Google search on how to remove the skunk smell. It was recommend to use peroxide,  baking soda and a drop of dish soap. I left my dog outside,  and grabbed a bucket. I quickly mixed solution in a bucket and grabbed a rag. I gave my dog a sponge bath outside with this solution. She now smells like a skunk again,  I was very disappointed,  I am returning the shampoo,  waste of time and money.

source_doc: My teeth squeak all the time now. My teeth squeak all the time now. Not in a cheesey mouse way or a "squeaky clean", but whenever I eat anything they start squeaking. It is the most uncomfortable thing ever and I only used two of the packets (one of the rapid ones and one of the normal) two weeks apart. Basically feels like the equivalent of nails going down a chalkboard but with your teeth.My teeth were never very sensitive and I would die for them to be super white so when I saw the deal on Black Friday, I HAD to cop. I was super excited to potentially see results, but after the two I used that obviously had no results, I was hoping that I could at least keep using them to try to get them to lift. However, for some reason a few days after my last strips I craved almonds. And that is when I first found out how teeth squeaking feel like. I thought I was going insane and looked it up and sure enough, almonds do make some people's teeth squeak. But it wouldn't stop after that. Just eating certain foods will make my teeth squeak and it made life a little more unenjoyable. Literally would have felt a little better if my teeth lifted a little bit. Thanks, Crest.

source_doc: Decent, feels like you need a lot though. Thus works a lot like your average face masks. You definitely see a brightness to your skin immediately after use. I have found 8 dollar ones of different brands that have 3 times more, and work the same as this, so the value just hits in the middle for me. This is something I would definitely order again, if it came in higher quantity, but until it does, I can save money by shopping in store for other brands that give the near same effect. This will be something I definitely will check in on to see if I can get a deal ever though, so it's better than some out there.

source_doc: Pretty good vs regular melatonin. I use melatonin sometimes when I'm having issues sleeping so when I saw this was 20 mg I decided I would have to try them.  When I was setting down for the night I popped one of these pills and waited for the magic.  It took about 15 minutes and I was out out for the night.  I did notice the next morning I wasn't as groggy as I had been with just plain melatonin (guess that's the magnesium)  so I like these more that the usual melatonin I get.  The taste and smell are n/a to me as I just open it and pop it in with a drink of water.  The pills are a bit big so I would use water with them.  All in all, I like these for sleepless nights and they will be my go-to from now on.

I have always thought that I would never have any reason to own my own karaoke machine, but now that I do, I can tell you that I can find a reason to own one almost every week. It is a party machine. It has been to the beach and back it did well. It sounds good, it gets loud, and the two microphones that it comes with are a cinch to use. They are up and running in less than a minute after I power up the speaker. It comes with a smartphone holder so that you can display a song's lyrics as you sing. The speaker rolls on two wheels, and it has a pull-out handle like a rolling suitcase. I have had a lot of fun using this machine and I have had zero problems with it. If you are looking for a karaoke machine, this is a good choice.

source_doc: Going back to knipex. Long story short, I tried to use these, and they weren’t for me. After cutting what turned out to be a hot wire thanks to sloppy wiring in the past, I discovered these after watching a video recommending them.  I thought the pliers would be sort of a two tools in one for my tool belt.  If I need to cut a heavy gauge wire, the button would give me additional leverage without going back to my tools or carrying one more tool around.  What happened instead was the 85% of the time I was just cutting 10, 12 or 14 ga romex that the pliers were awkward in my hand and about half the time locked shut.  It would turn  a no look grab from tool belt, cut and return to tool belt into a grab, fiddle, cut, return.  I don’t have small hands but I am certainly not palming basketballs either (typically size L glove). The wihas were bulkier than my knipex cutters. The difference was a tool that took little thought was replaced with a tool that just didn’t fit or feel right.  When I was removing some old chain link fence, I appreciated the extra leverage but how often do I do that.After trying them for a month, I finally just went back to my knipex cutters.  Maybe I didn’t give these a fair shake, but I really don’t like using tools that offer me no benefit.

source_doc: A pleasant surprise! I have to admit to being skeptical about this head wrap. I fully expected it to feel too tight or too heavy, but I was pleasantly surprised by how comfortable it is to wear.While it does feel heavy when you hold it, I didn’t find it too heavy when it was on my head. And though it’s tight, it wasn't too tight. It stays in place well, so if you choose to be up and about while wearing it, it shouldn’t slip down. It’s possible to pull it down over your eyes or leave it above your eyes, whatever best suits you. Personally, when I have a headache, I want the cooling relief over my eyes.Since it’s winter here and was below zero when my package was delivered, even though I took it from the drivers hand, the head wrap arrived cold. I’ve realized it always feels sort of cool to the touch, but I keep in the freezer as I like it colder. I haven’t tested it in the microwave since I don’t intend on using it that way.

source_doc: Great office chair! This seems like a nicely made computer chair. I am not very good at putting things together, but I managed to get this chair together all by myself! It suggests having two people put it together, and I agree that two people would make things much easier! I didn't have an issue until I tried to put the back of the seat on. I just couldn't get it in the right spot because I needed two hands to screw the bolts in. It took awhile, but I got it!The chair is very sturdy and the seat is very comfortable! The neck support is nice. The only issues I noticed were some of the wheels wouldn't roll as I pushed it back to my office. I assume with use, these wheels will start working. Also, I had planned on using it for my bar-height desk, but it is a few inches too short, so I will have to find another use for it. I think I assumed it would adjust that high, but I should have looked at the measurements.

source_doc: Skeptical at first, but I will not play without them again! I had just seen these grips on social media when a friend who had a set  recommended I give them a try. I was skeptical at first, but after my first three-hour gaming session, I will never play without them again.I play Fortnite almost every night, often for a few hours at a time. Usually my hands get sweaty after about an hour or so, but that did not happen with c2 Gripz, even after three hours. I bought the mediums, and my hands fit perfectly around the contoured grooves. source_doc: DIY, Save the mony. The detailer's wanted $1300. I watched 15 different YouTube Videos then decided on Adams. I do have a Quick Jack which made it a bit easier with the car lifted. It was easier than I thought ( I did do my homework). I took my time, started in a less noticeable spot and off to the races. I did have another advantage the car was freshly painted, I waited 3 weeks for the paint to gas off and I was done in 4 hours. It is a Miata MX5 a bit smaller than most cars. I left it in the garage for 24 hours before driving it. The first wash left beads of water and I dried the car with a 550 CFM leaf blower. Didn't even need a towel. I save me some big bucks and felt really good doing it myself.

source_doc: A solid and well-made gate. I have pretty much the same gate (different company) but without the cat door. I didn't know they even made gates with cat doors! I was thinking of all sorts of different things I could do to create a safety barrier but not lock the cats out. I didn't want to actually have to install a door and then cut a whole and install a cat door. I was excited when I ran across this product, and was hoping it was something of good quality (like my other gate). I was pleased when this arrived as it was quite heavy (a good thing) and is made with some sort of solid metal (can't be bent). I like that the cat door can be left open, or it can be locked. I admit when I installed my first gate it was a bit confusing as I wanted to get it right, but the manual that this came with is really helpful in it's detail and pictures. It helps I've already made an installation like this before, but even if I hadn't I appreciate the instructions. I will still use them. I don't remember how much I paid for the non-cat gate, but it was definitely more expensive than this. I'm glad they make a product like this!

source_doc: Deathadder without the wire! I've tried different brands/models of mice but have cumulatively used a Deathadder for over 7 years. I've always been too scared to pull the trigger on wireless mice because I had a bad experience with one and I'm not a fan of charging things constantly but the feel, the performance, everything, is amazing. I absolutely love it! It's exactly like my Deathadder Elite but without the wire.The only thing I will say is that I was disappointed with the battery life. I game much anymore and just casually hang out on my computer on days off from work. I also have the power saving mode set to 5 minutes because I'll go AFK to clean or hang out with my dogs often, so I'm not using it a ton. I guess I just expected a little more. The product advertises a "70 hour life", which I know is on the high end, but I expected more. Overall, I love this mouse and don't mind charging it for the convenience of not having a wire anymore.

source_doc: Back to basic, it’s what works! Who ever said newer and more technical is better was wrong. When I had my daughter 20 years ago we used the basic bulb sucker at home but this style in the hospital where I worked as a nursing student. I had my second child this year and saw that nasal aspirators had advanced, they’re electric with lights and sounds now. I of course got one immediately but when my baby got his first stuffy nose I came to realize they don’t offer very much suction and it was more work than it was worth. I tried a few others before going back to the basics. I remembered the one at the hospital working better than my bulb sucker so when I saw this I decided to try one more. This nasal aspirator works great! It has wonderful suction and I like that you control just how much. There aren’t a ton of parts that need cleaned afterward and nothing has to be done before using it in the middle of the night with a scared crying baby. You can tell it’s made with quality material and the little etching of the bunny is a cute addition. I’m very happy with this purchase and relieved I have a way of helping my baby breathe easier.

I cannot believe how long it has lasted and even that it traveled through each room so that when I came back from walking my dog and opened the door I immediately smelled the clean fresh scent of Gardenia Lily. I am a home fragrance fanatic and have tried many many products but this one has surpassed them all. I usually use a room spray and within half an hour the scent is completely gone so for this to last hours is amazing. Now that I know what this can do, I know I will only need a spray or two so this bottle is going to last a very very long time. I was wondering why this bottle of essential oil was at this price point but now I know. It's also 100% pure essential oil with no water. I can't wait to try it in a diffuser.

source_doc: Not a fan of the built in XLR cable. The boom stand itself works great. It is a good value for the money. The only thing I wasn't a fan of was the built in XLR cable it comes with. I am an Electrical Engineer and I tested this cable myself and can see that using a 150 ohm XLR preamp test on my desktop setup, I can see that my whole setup puts out a noise floor of about -100dB, which is extremely good. But it wasn't until I plugged in the XLR cable that my noise floor went up about 20dB. That is a lot for a cable and when I turned my gain up all the way to see if my hypothesis was correct, it was picking up radio interference from a local radio station, but barely could hear it. This means that the shielding on the wire itself has a fault somewhere or the wires themselves aren't balanced and not twisted pair. After I plugged in my own XLR cable that I had from a good source, I immediately saw my noise floor jump back up to -99dB and could hear no interference anymore. Just letting people know, that if you do expect to use this boom stand, make sure you also buy an XLR cable that is good quality. Now, I don't know if maybe I got a faulty cable, but it is something I wanted to warn people about.

source_doc: Best value for the price. I like the Old Mother Hubbard minis.  They're the perfect size for rewarding my dogs (I have large dogs).  I appreciate that the ingredients are better than many of the comparable treats, such as Milk Bones, and yet the price is more reasonable than brands like Blue.  My dogs are eager to be treated with them, so they must taste good.  As I stated, I have large dogs, so we do go through them somewhat quickly.  For this reason, I buy the 6lb boxes.  I get more for the cost.  I do feel like these could be better packaged.  The box isn't tightly sealed, just taped along the middle.  The biscuits are in a large plastic bag inside the box which isn't sealed either.  I do worry that these could easily be contaminated by their surrounding environment.  It would not be difficult for a mouse to crawl under the flap of the box and get inside the bag of biscuits.  Definitely something I think the manufacturer should consider.  When I get mine, I fill the treat jar and then store the remaining in the deep freezer until I need them.  (My German Shepherd is allergic to storage mites, so this helps me negate that issue.)

source_doc: So great for travel. This is such a creative idea for a traveling mom. I got it for an upcoming cruise because I thought I would be pumping and this would be perfect, but I ended up drying up too early. I was still able to use it for little visits to grandma's house, etc. I like that it has little separate branches for all the parts. I probably could have used a couple more, but it worked well. I did not personally like the silicone bottle brush that was included so I just brought my own regular bottle brush. I did really like that it came with a small soap bottle. I think this would be perfect for a working mom who is pumping and doesn't want to leave their pump stuff all over the icky shared kitchen or something.

source_doc: It’s okay. It’s a starter kit, so it will give you what you need for a quick start up. I purchased Quick Start and Stress Coat+ instead of using the conditioner provided with the tank and they worked very well. Within a few hours of adding those in and running the filter, my water was ready.I’m not a fan of the filter at all, it’s loud, creates a strong current, and it doesn’t do the best job of cleaning the water (the sole thing a filter is supposed to do). Based on previous reviews it’s not reliable so within a week of having it I decided to replace it with an inexpensive, but much more reliable, sponge filter that doesn’t create a current. Happy water, happy fish.The lights are decent, though I wish they were dimmable. There are cheap options for dimmable lights with a timer that can be submerged, and I will be using those instead.The instructions for this tank mention a provided heater. There isn’t one provided, which I think is better as I found a heater that reads the water temperature and it’s keeping my betta very happy.Overall, the tank is decent and a huge upgrade from the 2.5 gallon I had before. With the money I spent, I could’ve purchased a bigger tank since I replaced everything else but now I know for the future.

source_doc: Really Works to Prevent Color Bleeding. I usually separate my whites from darker clothing out of fear that the dye from the dark clothing will stain the white. So I was excited to try this product.Basically the sheets look like fabric softener sheets, only they're meant for "grabbing" the color shed by darker clothes and preventing them from bleeding onto the lighter ones. I dropped 2 sheets in my load of laundry, started the machine, and added detergent.To test the product, I threw in a pair of burgundy colored corduroy pants that explicitly said "Wash separate from light colors" and even stated "dye may bleed." I threw them into the same wash as my lighter colored shirts and socks.After the wash was done, I saw that the two "color grabber" sheets had turned gray (they were originally white). They had absorbed the color and when I checked my clothing, I saw no color "bleeds."Now, I haven't tested it with a hot water wash, but for the cold water wash, they definitely work. I love it. Usually I have to separate the whites from the other clothing and it wastes money because the all-white bundle is usually small and could easily fit with the rest of the clothing's washer. But I had always had to separate. Not anymore! I can toss one of these sheets in and it will prevent any color bleeding.Great product.

source_doc: Seems like a good collar. My cats needed new collars and I thought I'd give this one a try.  I ordered the cloud print and it's cute.  No issues with sizing the collar to what I needed and I did try pulling apart on it to ensure it would "break away" if need be and it did come apart with a fairly good tug.  My cats are indoor cats so I doubt it will be put to the test, but would want to make sure it would just in case.  I do have to say I don't care for the bell.  My cat's last collar had a bell and it really wasn't noisy unless he was really running.  This bell is very noisy.  It's a smaller sound, kind of a tinny sound.  But I could tell my cat did not like it.  At least for the first few days he was constantly messing around with his neck like he was trying to find the bell.  He never did that with his last collar.  I was actually getting ready to take it off but it's been about a week and he seems used to it now so I'll leave it be for a bit longer and see.  But I do wonder if it's still driving him nuts.  I may still remove it at some point.

source_doc: Looks can be deceiving.... I really hate this clock.I'll start with what I like about it (which isn't much).It looks beautiful, very elegant and classy. Nice and large, easy to see from a distance.It keeps the perfect time. Doesn't make a sound.That's it. That's all I like.Now what I hate about this thing...It's super flimsy! I thought it might shatter just by putting two AA batteries in it.It's made of acrylic which is no big deal, it just makes it really lightweight. I doubt anyone who sees it on your wall would know that it wasn't real wood, but still feels like cheap plastic to me.The pendulum.... ohemgeeeee I really HATE that thing! It doesn't move AT ALL! I have tried everything under the sun to get that thing moving and nope, it just sits there staring at me like it's claimed it's victory by not budging. It honestly makes no sense, it only goes on there one way. And the pendulum is the only metal component in this clock. Everything else is plastic.Overall, it makes me mad just looking at it. I'm glad I got it on the vine because I definitely wouldn't have paid $50 for it. That would have been an instant return! It's all plastic, super flimsy, but looks really nice and does keep time. That's the only reason I gave it two stars. You can definitely find something much nicer for the same price elsewhere.

source_doc: Really liked them, but they would not charge. I really liked these lanterns. They flashlight option was extremely bright. The big downside is the charging. Upon receiving them, I plugged them both in. A blue light came on for about 5 seconds and then disappeared. I assumed this meant that they were fully charged. I took them camping and they started fading before the end of the first night. The next day I plugged them both in for about 3 hours apiece. The same thing happened when I plugged them in, a blue light for about 5 seconds then it disappeared. No indication if they were actively charging or fully charged. After 3 hours of charging apiece, I tried using them for my 2nd night of camping. As soon as I turned them, they died within a minute as if they hadn’t been charged at all. I returned them. These lanterns failed me on my camping trip. I can’t have an unreliable light source that doesn’t given any indication at all of charging or battery status. It’s a shame because I really liked the outside of the charging issues..

source_doc: Probiotic toothpaste. I am a huge fan of using probiotics for all types of products, so I was happy to try this product. It has a more delicate flavor than the toothpastes I’m accustomed to using, from America. There’s a subtle mint and sweet flavor, I found it refreshing. I don’t expect it to whiten my teeth… I use whitening strips for that, and even with those, it requires regular use for my teeth to get whiter. I like using whitening toothpastes though, sort of as daily maintenance. But I’ve never tried a whitening toothpaste on its own that actually made my teeth whiter.One thing I did notice is that I have a sensitive spot on my teeth that I started feeling after using this for a few days. I normally use Sensodyne because of tooth sensitivity. And the sensodyne definitely keeps that at bay. So I probably wouldn’t repurchase this for that reason, and also because it’s pretty expensive (currently $49 for a 3.52oz tube). But I did enjoy the other aspects of this toothpaste.

I DO think that it should come with at least two of this manufacturers small tissue packets though.  It would not cost that much more to include them with the tissue holders. That works and cutting regular size tissues will save me money in the future when I need to refill my tissue holders!  I am glad that I purchased these holders, as these holders will prevent us from searching for our tissue boxes that we normally have in the back seat. source_doc: This is going to take some practice for all three of us! After getting a second puppy in our life, I wanted the ability to take them both out for walks together and have at least one hand free  When I saw this I thought how fabulous this would be!  It arrived and I hooked the three of us up.  My older puppy is fairly good at leading alone.  The puppy, is even better!  She is a natural heeler!  I thought it would be a breeze!  Yeah, didn't go as I expected.  I quickly felt like I was the monkey in the middle with dogs going every direction and pulling me in the middle!  Then the fun, I stopped to get them under control and they each wrapped around me like some kind of insane doggie butterfly cocoon!  I managed to get control of the beasts, unwind myself and grabbed those broncs by the short handles of those leads!  I proceeded to walk ourselves home to get the regular leashes and I will use the regular leashes on this fanny pack until they get the hang of it better.  I think it was the extra bungie stretch they had that allowed them to go insane!Positive note:  The pack, the leads and all components held up great to the insane dance these dogs put me through!  I like being able to carry their treats with me and the other pouch for potty bags, keys, etc!

source_doc: DO NOT BUY THESE. these are absolute garbage unless you just want to play by yourself. they are so buggie i have to keep going back in and play with the audio settings in my XBOX series x MULTIPLE TIMES per session. I have 2 accounts on my Xbox and i use the same headset for each (for a high level and low level character in a particular game that won't let you have multiple characters), this screws up the headset every time i switch back and forth (others can hear me but i can't hear them, so i have to go into xbox settings and start over). then there's an annoying occurrence where if i play alone the audio is really decent- not great but decent. as soon as my wife invites me to a party her voice is super loud and i can't hear the game. these headphone lock you out of the normal chat mixer and force you to use the volume dials on the headset- but the problem is the volume doesn't change. I have my wife screaming at me and i can't hear the game, the games music or my guns shooting- so i smashed these pieces of garbage on my table. total garbage. the XBOX official ones were the same price, but they were not available so i got these, that was a hundred bucks i really regret spending.

source_doc: I put this thing through the ringer. Reviewing "Wahl Color Pro Cordless Rechargeable Hair Clipper & Trimmer – Easy Color-Coded Guide"I'm a gym rat / exercise buff with bodybuilding background that puts this thing to full-body use.  I've now bought four of these things over the past 3-5 years (same exact one I'm reviewing here), and it's fantastic.  I keep the blade cleaned and oiled, and I *always* keep a blade guard on it when not in use so as not to scratch or full the metal blades.  My main point is that if you take care of it, it will last pretty decently.  The reason I've bought four or five of these is because I use them like crazy (yes, full body shaving, including haircuts).  Compared to older products that I bought in my youth, I like the wide blade for greater surface area (faster job done), and the variety of guard sizes (as I also cut the kids' hair).  Oh, as to why I've bought several of these it's because they don't sell just replacement blades--at least not that I can find.  Therefore, for the cheap price, I just go ahead and buy a new one.  Anyway, I like them and recommend them.  If you're a professional barber, you probably would use something else, but I wanted battery powered so no cord.  I also try not to get water into the mechanism.

source_doc: Amazing Powder for the extra coverage I need! Airspun Loose Powder Translucent Extra Coverage- I’ve found a gem with this powder. At first I thought it would be too light for my skin but it’s not the case at all. Other powders I’ve used in the past have been beige. This powder amazingly blends into my skin beautifully. After my morning routine of cleansing, toning, vitamin C serum & moisturizer I then use L’Oreal Magic Erase Primer which is the only primer that controls my very oily skin. Once my face is set I apply this powder. This sets my face for an entire day! I apply it before 7am & it’s still looking great at 7pm. Liquid foundation has never worked for me due to my oily skin. I also have scarring from acne I had when I was a teenager into my 20’s. This powder falls nicely into place eliminating the look of this on my face. I love it! There is a lot of powder that comes in this container. For the price it’s amazing. A puffer comes with it but I use my makeup brush to pick the powder up to apply it. Yes, there is a scent to it. This doesn’t bother me but if you’re sensitive to fragrance this wouldn’t be for you. Otherwise I’d say with the low price it’s worth trying. From my personal experience I definitely recommend it!

source_doc: Finally, the perfect heating blanket! I've been looking for a heating blanket for my bed, when I found one, I really liked it. However, the middle of the blanket would not warm up. I sent the blanket back and asked for a replacement since I reasoned that there might just be a problem with it. The identical action was taken by the second blanket. I subsequently bought another blanket, but I didn't like it because the coils only allowed it to heat up in the middle, not on either side. Even when I bought a fourth heating blanket, it still would not become hot enough. I was about to give up when I decided to give this one a last go.I am very happy I did. Only setting number medium  on this heated blanket keeps me toasty. It becomes unbearably hot if it’s on high. . Not only is the temperature control excellent. It's incredibly soft. I sincerely hope you enjoy the blanket as much as I do and my four-legged luvies.

source_doc: Fun. I bought this in November, tomorrow it will be January and I have yet to finish the game as I’m having so much fun exploring and dinking around as I play. I wasn’t sure how I’d like the tera evolution deal but it’s not bad but I don’t really use the feature although I do enjoy the battles against the tera Pokémon too. I do wish I could customize more of what my character is wearing as the school uniform kinda sucks and I love customizations so much but I am glad I can change between seasonal wear. The new Pokémon are interesting and I’m enjoying learning about them too.

source_doc: Just as described! My machine was delivered Feb 4th. I started using it that day. Easy assembly. Only took 30 min. I use it about 3-4 times a week. 1st couple days I didn't use any bands to get used to the machine, then I started using 1 of them. I rotate excercise, 1 day I do 200 squats with only 1 band. Next day I do 50 squats no band, 50 with 1 band, anther 50 with 2 bands and back to 1 band to complete my 200 squats. I hit my zone minutes but can get used to it very easily which is why I keep switching up the routine. I am on a calorie deficit and this is the only exercise I do. I plan to try using the deadlift "feature" of this machine this week to add more workouts. I love it. Worth the purchase to me!Editing to add: I started using the deadlify feature this week and definitely will continue using it.  You can feel the burn where the squats wasn't!!

source_doc: Excellent lunch bag! When shopping for some type of lunch bag item, I stumbled across the Eco-Friendly lunch bag. I liked everything I read about it so I decided to order. On the inside upper lid there is a section (with a zipper to close the section off) I was able to put 2 small box juices and a small ziploc bag of grapes. It is so light weight and the outside material reminds me of denim. I truly believe you will love it as much as I do!

source_doc: It’s fun and enjoyable. I’ve never picked up a guitar in my life until this was delivered so I can’t attest to playability or quality. I did swap out the strings when I got it but more because I wanted to learn how to do it than any perceived problem with the strings that came with it. I can say I have enjoyed experimenting and learning with this guitar.  I paired it with an “Orange” amp and despite not having a clue what I’m doing have been able to replicate sounds like ‘old school’ heavy metal to clear/clean tones that could pass for country or blues if played by someone who knew more than 2 cords. I suspect in trained or experienced hands this guitar would be a good, but not great, guitar.A few things I did notice…1. There are some exposed wires coming out from under one of the pickups and the middle pickups are not level. 2. There is some discoloration on the body of the guitar  3. The tuning peg for the high E is finicky and sometimes feels unresponsive which can make tuning a pain.For what I paid, I didn’t expect perfection, and I have no idea if the uneven pickups impact playability or sound quality, the remainder are cosmetic or just frustrating. I think this probably represents a solis starter guitar or a good rehearsal/travel guitar for more experienced players.

source_doc: Just What I Needed. I was looking for a bread cutting guide that cut all the bread the same size, easy to store in a small space and easy to clean.  I did not want the lovely bamboo guides because  they were spaced to accommodate 3 sizes of slices on a somewhat small grid so then I would have to move the bread after every so many cuts in order to have them be the same size.  The key word I was interested in is "easy".  With this guide if I want thicker slices all I need to do is skip a space -- easy! Used this bread cutting guide today and am quite happy with it and would purchase it again. It cleans up easily -- just a quick wipe with soap and water.  However it's crumb catching ability is not great. I just place it on a jelly roll pan and cut away.  If one is giving this item as a gift it, comes in a very nice box.  If you order a white bread guide do not be alarmed if the box shows the red guide on the outside.  I think the red guide just shows up better on the box.  This guide is so much better than the Presto one I had before. I would purchase this guide again.

source_doc: dryer nice, but the red/yellow reset/test buttons keeps faulting. The dryer works & I like it, but each time I go to use it I find the red/yellow reset/test buttons have faulted and the dryer won't power on until I reset.  I've tried it in several different outlets & using a surge strip, same result when NOT in use.  I've also tested another hair dryer in the same outlet, no issue.  I have contacted the manufacturer.  They asked me to send a bunch of photos, which I did, along with the receipt.  Then they asked me to send more photos in order for them to activate the warranty. They asked me to cut the cord & send photos of that.  I don't have the original box, so I can't return to Amazon.  As of now, I just unplug it and don't leave it on when not in use.  I guess I'll buy a different brand so I have something to use until they respond.  The way the manufacturer is giving me the run around is the reason for the 2 stars.

source_doc: Very useful and best of all, small and light. Talk about timing, this battery came just in time for when I was due in a VR meeting and I forgot to charge the headset.  The battery fastens very easily to the side of the headstrap, but I wonder how long the battery strap will last.  I pulled it tight to prevent sagging, and it seemed like I might stretch out the strap holes and eventually it might break apart.  Aside from that, the battery worked perfectly.  I was in VR for two hours using this battery, but I will say that I think it charged my HMD very slowly.  I didn't think to look at the battery status until it had 94%, and it seemed like it took forever to get to 100%.  Then again, I was using it at the same time so maybe that's normal.This battery is light and small, much unlike the 3rd party batteries that I used to have to wear for the Quest 1.  I would highly recommend this battery to anyone who needs one for their headset.

source_doc: Awesome Poor Man's Peloton. I purchased this about a year ago to use as a cheap alternative to a Peloton. Assembly was super easy. I added a bluetooth Wahoo cadence tracker, my Apple Watch for heart rate, and my iPad fit perfectly on top to stream the Peloton app. The only thing I cannot replicate is the resistance and I just go by how hard they say it should be, it works for me. I love it. I have a quiet room it is tucked away in that I can work out in and have had absolutely zero problems other than the infamous seat squeak which only happens if I fidget. I am just at the point that cages are getting annoying and I am going to put clipless pedals on but the cages worked fine. For reference, I am 5'1", 200lbs, and have never broken a pedal standing to ride or had any clunking noises. I do feel like I could use one more tiny click lower on the seat to perfect the alignment, or farther forward but not to the point it is uncomfortable.

source_doc: Outstanding ironing board! I never thought I would use ironing board and outstanding in one sentence, but this one definitely stands out.I was hesitant to order it because of the higher price. I never paid anything near this much for an ironing board lol.So why did I order it?First I saw the nice attachment with the little compartments. I immediately thought I could use it for scissors, tape measure and pins since I usually cut fabric on my ironing board due to lack of space in my craftsroom.Then I read that the ironing board is extra wide, another plus for cutting fabric or doing other crafts.I also noticed that you can pull it up to 36 inches which is counter top height and is easy on my back when I'm ironing.Of course I also read the positive reviews and eventually decided to order it.After unpacking and admiring the awesome attachment, the great quality, the sturdiness and the extra cover, I set it up in my craftsroom.I noticed that it was a little wobbly (it's our floor) so I put a piece of styrofoam underneath one of the legs.I read the description which came with it to make sure I didn't miss anything and guess what!The feet have built in stabilizers which are adjustable so no need to put anything underneath!It really can't get any better!An outstanding product for sure!5 stars from me. ☆☆☆☆☆

source_doc: Bought 2, here’s my opinion. So I bought two when it was on sale for $18 each. I bought one as a gift and one for myself. I asked the other person how it was and he said it worked great. I had mine in my car for over 6 months and I just used it last week. I noticed the low air indicator light was on so I plugged it into my car. I noticed it has three different setting of pressure. I put it on psi and it showed that it was low. I let it run till it got to my cars psi recommended level and turned it off. There is only one caveat, I’m not sure how accurate it is. I also had a handheld pressure tester and it was old and it showed a different number. When I got into the car and drove for a little the tire indicator was off. So in essence it did its job. And well worth the investment.

source_doc: Please don’t try and use these for more than a few months. These have been great, I got a set , then had a another set gifted to us for our daughter less than a year ago. They stain with some pasta sauces which I thought was the only downside. If you’re using a dishwasher DISPOSE OF THEM AFTER A MONTH OR SO!! I noticed my daughters requests for dinner changed. She went from eating everything I made, steak, chicken, pork, spinach, quiche, to over time she would eat just pb&j or soup. I tried one of her spoons and they’re either porous and they hold on to the dishwasher chemicals or they’re leeching themselves. Like burns your throat. DO NOT USE THESE THINGS IN A DISHWASHER.I use cascade in a 2 year old Frigidaire dishwasher, I don’t use high heat so I’m not cooking them a couple times a week. It isn’t the only way I wash these utensils, it’s 50/50 with hand washing but something is not ok. Please ONLY use these short term. I thought I was doing something good getting a recycled item but I feel like I screwed up getting these.

source_doc: Photophobia no more. I am extremely sensitive and picky when it comes to lighting. If a room is too bright I can't stay in there for too long as I feel like a fish in a tank and can't think. A perfect room has a range of dimmable light options but unfortunately my desk space didn't. Desperate to find a solution that kept me from leaving my work space, I stumbled upon this simple modern looking option. I have used it everyday since receiving it. I hardly ever turn on the lights to my room and instead opt to use this little lamp instead. I love all the different options I can choose from depending on what I am feeling. I also love to use it to do my makeup as one of the settings resembles daylight. This versatile lamp is very worth it for the price point. I am glad I took a chance on it!

source_doc: Only oil I use. I am glad that I have been able to buy this oil from this same vendor for years. Unfortunately I opted for a food that is heavily gravied,  next time it will be a pate. I used a pill crusher to mask the pill. I think that one of them did not get a full dose. He ateat least 85% of his dose. What he didn't finish the rest of his food his sister did, she has fleas too. Now, I'm just waiting to find dead fleas. I guess my eye got in the way of its jump. LOL

We decided to use a pair of scissors, instead of a knife, to make a small cut and then slowly tore open each package.  I let the velvety-soft sofa bed rest, unzipped, while hanging over the top of a Lazy boy chair. I then noticed the nonslip coating on the bottom, which will prevent future slips into and out of the bed.  I positioned the foam pad on our sofa.  Both covers are thankfully machine washable.  This is necessary because our doodle does get stinky.  I waited about four days until I put them together.  My 50 lb. doodle loved the velvety-soft bed immediately!  The thick, supportive foam felt good, and it was the perfect size, after all.  I'm glad I ordered one.

source_doc: Excellent quality and lovely zippered case. I think another reviewer said these weren’t made of real memory foam, but when I compared it to my other memory foam pillows, it was definitely the same quality.I also like the fact that they were no offgassing smells when I resuscitated the pillow from being compressed in a small box.The thing with these pillows, and I have been using them for years from different  companies, is you have to try them for yourself. There are subtle differences in the dimensions of each one, and our bodies are differently designed, so you just have to experiment.I tried it with, and without the inner insert, without the insert it was just a little too floppy, even though it felt comfortable to lie on.The only other thing I want to mention is the case, while it is really beautiful quality and aesthetically designed, is a little too long for the actual pillow I received. When I see a little, I mean about an inch.This doesn’t really affect anything, so I didn’t take any stars away for it, it’s just some thing you might wanna know when events. I think it’s very good quality and looked as if it would last a long time. That said, you can find less expensive models that might do the trick for you, but I doubt they will be queen-size, they will probably be standard size.

source_doc: Looks and feels great. I thought I'd try these in my old, 2010 Prius after having replaced the original leather with  cheap vinyl seating elements. The vinyl was cheap but professionally installed. It looked ok, but did not wear well. So, I thought I'd give these a try.  Now, I wish I'd known about Karcle before I replaced the original leather.  I'm more than pleased with this product; I actually learned something from the experience.Because my Prius has heated seats, installation was a little more difficult. I went through contortions securing the elastic ties that go beneath the seat and hold the bottom element in place. But if your seats aren't heated and there aren't a lot of electronics under them, you won't have this problem. In any case, after a brief struggle, I got both pieces on. They look great and feel very comfortable.  The material--nappa leather--appears very durable. It's supposed to be washable. Time will tell, but right now, I'm in love with these.  I didn't need to replace the rear seating because nobody every sits there.Update:  after a few weeks driving, I've come to love these seat covers. They look great and feel better than the third rate vinyl that was professionally installed. No, they're not as tightly fit as they vinyl, but they look and feel a lot better.Update: After a few weeks of driving I like these seat covers even more than I did when I first put them on.

source_doc: Excellent mid-size carrying case. The reason I got this case for my Steam Deck is I wasn't happy with the velcro on the JSAUX case and had a couple other issues with it where I didn't feel like my deck was properly secured. This fella however solves all those issues. First, this case is a LOT bigger than the JSAUX case, the top is as wide as the bottom. There's a massive top pocket that you could shove a small Nintendo Switch carrying case into but otherwise it's perfect for batteries, controllers, docks, etc. I really wasn't expecting it to be that spacious! The bottom compartment isn't quite as big as the JSAUX one but I was able to cut out a slot for my charging brick using a boxcutter so no big deal, the interior material cut very easily. The protection for this felt wayyy better than the JSAUX case. The straps are excellent and the velcro is very good. The interior is also a bit padded which feels nice. It has microsd storage slots as well as fullsize SD storage slots. I was worried about the microSD's falling out so I kept them in their SD adapters anyways. The only feature I couldn't quite get working was the kickstand strap so I just shoved that down in the bottom and put a different kickstand in the top storage so I have one if I ever need it.

source_doc: Very sturdy! I have high hopes for the longevity of this dish drainer. What do we moved to a smaller place I decided to use just a draining mat figuring I would roll it up between uses. So 2 and 1/2 years later there are still always dishes on the mat so I decided to just get an actual dish drainer like I should have done when we moved okay. It helped with the decision that every time my daughter's boyfriend helps wash dishes he breaks something from making a leaning Tower of Dishes.When I took this out of the box I was surprised and pleased at the weight of it.  There is no flex in it, the metal is strong and sturdy, stainless steel not plastic coated cheap metal.There is also the added advantage of extendable arms on either end so you can position it over to the sink to drain directly into the sink. I'm not sure I will use that aspect very often, but I am very pleased with this product.It is a little smaller than I expected, but that's on me because I didn't check the measurements before I ordered. source_doc: Fender Mexico Surprised Me. I have another Mexican Starr I bought many years ago but this is a huge step up in quality. It seems many higher end manufacturers are moving some of their production to Mexico which I think is driving competition. I bought this as used but in very good condition. Very pleased. I had bought the same guitar from Musicians Friend which they sold as a New instrument which was returned. That one was abused so I returned it and was happily surprised when Amazon had one left. The finish is great and I find no faults in quality so far. I also have several American made Strats which surprised me that Fender had an anniversary model made in Mexico but don’t let that fool you. The only big difference I find is this doesn’t have the nitrocellulose finish. I wish they had shipped it in a hard case but I’ll get one for it anyway. The gig bag is their better one but I prefer to protect my favored guitars. Overall I’d say this was a great purchase!

source_doc: Saved my back and knees! Hurray! I am at that age where sometimes I have to put off chores because I've used up my back or knees or feet for the day.I probably should have gotten something like this a few years ago.  This really is super usefule.  We have a small shower stall, but it was still super hard to get down to clean the floor.  Last time, I sort of tipped over after crouching down to scrub, I was kinda like a turtle on it's back, my leg muscles spasming as I tried to get up.This is so much easier, so far, I have only used the more abrasive scrubby attachment, I pour a little soft scrub, then cleaned the floor while leaning against the wall.  It was probably the most lazy shower clean I have ever experienced.The scrubbie is good at flat surfaces, but if you really need to get at a corner, you have to press really hard to get in there.  I don't know what the solution to that is.  After I was done cleaning the shower, I cleaned and rinsed the attachment and set it  on the top of the washing machine to dry before I put them away.The soft shamm-y attachment is a real conundrum.  I guess it could be used to clean mirrors or windows.  I will give a whirl next time.

source_doc: Fantastic reading glasses. I usually use bifocals but for some things just reading glasses are ok since the bifocals are expensive. source_doc: The formula has changed. I bought this product because I have used it before and loved it.  However something changed and it caused a mild allergic reaction.  I know that I have some allergies that often get labeled as “fragrance” in skin products so I normally test a new product on my wrist first.  I didn’t this time because I had used the product before, so I just immediately applied it to my whole face. source_doc: Excellent protection, no white cast, but sticky. I put Zinc Five-O Baby Mineral Sunscreen to the test against the mid-afternoon Arizona sun which is still super strong, even in winter. I can verify that it provides excellent sun protection with spf 50. Considering it is a zinc product I was surprised it didn't leave that tell-tale white cast that nobody likes but everybody puts up with to get that great protection. The product is thick, non-irritating, and has no real scent to speak of. After applying, it doesn't absorb into the skin (typical of zinc sunscreens), but it leaves a somewhat oily and sticky film that I found super annoying. Because it was a windy day, my long hair was blowing around and sticking to nearly every surface that I had applied sunscreen to. I also had some blowing sand and dirt stick to my arms. Despite this, the sunscreen provided excellent protection for the entire 60 minutes that I was outdoors. The second time I used it, I applied the product only to my face and neck and I followed up the application with a face powder to cut the stickiness, which seemed to do the trick. Because this is a sunscreen for babies, I imagine parents could apply corn starch afterwards if they find the stickiness to be problematic. I, however, will save this product for use poolside this summer because it provides excellent protection and that is really what is important.

source_doc: Amazing quality for a low price. I tested this lavalier microphone on a Zoom call where I wanted to stay connected with audio but leave the room completely. I was connected to the meeting through my cell phone, which I left in my office aimed at a chart when I roamed around my house. (Of course, I could have carried the phone with me during the Zoom meeting, but I was testing the audio at various distances.)  My Zoom meeting partner reported I sounded like I was sitting right in the room. Installing the receiver and microphone was a snap - the receiver plugs in to the charging port of the iPhone, and the light on that receiver blinks red until the microphone is turned on. When paired, the light on the receiver is a steady red (not blinking), and the microphone shines a steady green. The foam windscreens aren't necessary in the house but can be left on if that's the look you want. I am looking forward to using this lavalier when I record voice-over on my next PowerPoint lecture using my iPad.

source_doc: This gadget is freaking amazing! As it would happen, if things can go wrong, they will.  The day before I received a positive COVID test that not only knocked me on my ass, but the very next day the master bath toilet backed up.  I plunged and plunged, and plunged, and plunged to no avail.  So, I turned to Amazon and found this gadget. I thought it would be a rinkydink, use a couple of times before tossing into the garbage but to my surprise I was wrong.  I’m rarely wrong :).  In my now full on COVID ravaged body I easily assembled, pumped it up (29 pumps to be exact) shoved the gadget into the tank.  I kinda felt like Rambo as I pulled the trigger!  Yes, there is actual trigger.  To my surprise, the recoil felt like a shot a baby shotgun!  What I didn’t know is that I should have tried to cover the bowl because along with the recoil, a bunch of toilet water splashed back on me and the floor.  After I got over that shocker, I flushed and Wallace.  Whatever was stuck was gone.  It probably got blown to smithereens!  Run, and don’t hesitate to make this purchase!

source_doc: This is the leash I never knew I needed. I bought this to use with my dog's therapy dog vest - I need a 4' leash when working.  I also wanted the short loop so I could have the dog fully in control.This is very nice.  It's quite light, but strong.  Excellent quality clasp. My dog is on the small size (18"), and this is just perfect for when I am working him in places where I need really close control.  I usually use a 6' leash, held in my right hand, with the left controlling the shorter length.  However, the second handle just makes it much simpler - one less thing to juggle and more solid control.My dog's vest is red with black, so the black leash with the red flashes looks sharp.  I use it with the vest (like harness), with his standard collar, but also with a Gentle Leader when we are doing therapy work.  The light weight is important with a small dog with the Gentle Leader - I did not want to put weight on pressure on his delicate nose. I may change out the clasp for a slightly lighter one just to relieve some of the weight.Good product for a working dog - light but well made, well designed, and it seems durable.

source_doc: Okay, this filter is no joke. When I first found this filter, I was skeptical. A good filter, for a 75 gallon tank, that's under $30? No way. Not when we paid $100+ for our AquaTech. I was on the phone with my husband and he almost laughed when I told him the price and that I was going to try it out. He told me not to get my hopes up, there's no way it could be good. I was doing a partial water change and I knew I'd be disturbing a lot of sediment and our old filter was on its last legs, so I decided to take a chance.Y'all. When I tell you this little thing WORKS. It cleaned my filthy tank water overnight. Within the first hour I could see a massive difference and by morning? Almost crystal clear. All the filters were filthy within a day from just how much crap they'd sucked up. Oh, and the output is so strong I had to use the little L adjuster pipe to aim the output flow at the side of the tank, because it was creating too strong of a current for my littler tetras. This thing is amazing. I'm buying another one just to put two in my tank to keep it even cleaner. Please note, I've had this thing for almost three months now and it's still going strong.

source_doc: WOW. I am no longer a Sacrete guy. I set a 4x4, 8 foot post using this product.  I made a hole 2 feet deep, 7 to 8 inch diameter.  One package of this stuff nearly filled the entire hole with the post centered in it.  Mixed it exactly as the instructions dictate. I was initially disappointed because the liquid I poured in only filled up a couple of inches.  I was using a 2-foot level to confirm the pole was remaining vertical and then I looked in the hole and it was more than half-way full up with foam and I could see it rising. In perhaps 5 minutes more, it was nearly completely full up on all four sides.  After 15 minutes I removed the straps I was using to hold the post in place, and light pressure on the sides of the post showed no give in the foam, it was solid enough to leave standing alone.  Incredibly easy compared to how I used to have to mix a bag of sacrete by hand and carry the 30 or 40 pounds around.  Wish I had another project needing another bag of this stuff so I could do it all again, it was well, "fun".

source_doc: Nice, Slim. I had my doubts.  But I like these.  The one I use most is holding olive oil.  I like the very thin spout, I have good control of how much oil I add to the pan. Obviously I don't need the one from the olive oil bottle so I use it to start plant cuttings, but "someone" in my house was enjoying it as a liquor shot glass before I co-opted it for horticultural use.

source_doc: Unbeatable great value cable. I got this as a temporary cable while I wait for an actual high quality one to come in. For those, you must either pay big or you wait a month to get it. Enter this cable:Less than 15 bucks, arrives the next day (for me,) and works great. The price and availability are unbeatable. How does the cable perform? I haven't been able to to detect any noise on the video or the audio. If there's audio hum, I geneuinly haven't noticed it. These are cheap so I'm sure they're hit or miss and I doubt the wires are individually shielded. But the one I received murders the composite cable I was using. I would even say it surpasses perfect s-video quality. It's sharp colorful rgb video.The cable feels and looks cheap, but it IS cheap. And you're definitely rolling the dice on the build quality here, but I can at least vouch that you'll potentially receive a solid cable that looks a million times better than composite.I might come back later and compare it to a high quality scart cable to note the differences, but I would say go ahead and give this one a try if you want to save some time and money. Bottom line: the cable I got looks great.

source_doc: Great item for the money fixed up my oil leak! I purchased this and was concerned about the low price.  I cleaned it out thoroughly looking for debri before proceeding with install and found none.From reading other "cheap" replacement oil filter housing reviews most folks advocated for replacing the oil and temp sending unit.  The last thing I want to do is strip the engine down as far as I did for one of those.  I went ahead and bought auto part store senders and replaced what was on here.  It may have worked fine I just didnt want to dig back in to the engine for them.You have to take off the upper and lower initakes to get to this.  I found over a quart of oil sitting on top of the engine that I had to clean out.  Once replaced and everything re-installed I am happy to report that I have used my inspecting camera and a simple "dip stick" to try to find oil under the intake and it has come back clean.  I put this in before Christmas so as of this review over a month and so far so good.Very happy that my oil leak is finally solved!

source_doc: Refused to connect. I had a lamp I wanted to use Alexa with and I have other older Kasa smart plugs that work fine.  My other bulbs were Lumiman and I thought I would try to make everything just Kasa.  So I ordered a Kasa smart bulb but it refused to connect.  I thought that maybe it was because the lamp was one of those metal swing-arm things, so I thought, well, I'll just get another Kasa plug instead and ordered a used set of 2.  They both refused to connect.  Thinking it was because they were used, I ordered 2 more new ones.  And, guess what, they refused to connect, too.  I tried everything with all of them.  Multiple tries and resets, moving the lamp all over the house and even right next to the router.  None of them would connect.  So I ordered another Lumiman bulb and, lo and behold, it connected right away with absolutely no issues.  2 stars is for the old plugs that actually worked.

source_doc: My dog loves them. I have a dog with heart disease that usually does not mind taking his pills but at times one may be too bitter so I got him these. As far as flavor, I have not tasted them but I can say that the hickory ones are the most liked by all my dogs. When I give my sick dog the pills, the others want the soft chew too, so I give them one  as a treat when they see me. Before I used to buy the chicken flavored ones and only my sick dog took them. The rest were not interested. They didnt smell. The hickory ones smell strong and like real human food. I almost want one from the smell. I like that they are soft and moist and do not crumble. For bigger pills, I cut them and put them in there and I can remold the little ball. Have not tried the peanut butter ones but I will stick to the Hickory as all my dogs love them.

source_doc: This made me extremely nauseous. I read the benefits of taking 400mcg of folic acid & decided to entail this in my daily vitamin regime. This may work well for some. For me I had a very bad reaction to it upon taking it the first day. Within 4 hours I became very nauseous. I had to leave work. I knew it was due to putting this new vitamin in my body. I’ve researched folic acid since & wanted to share that there can be side effects from taking it. In some cases one may experience nausea, black stool, constipation, loss of appetite, bloating or gas. I spoke to my Doctor about it. There was no type of adverse reaction with the other vitamins I was taking. It was simply my body didn’t like it. He did ask if I took it with a full glass of water & food, which I did. He said this was important. So a heads up if you’re considering to purchase for the first time. This may not be for you.  I do respect this brand of vitamin. Unfortunately I can’t receive the nice benefits gained by taking it.

source_doc: You're paying less for a reason. I've used wood glue many times. But in the past I've used gorilla glue, which has never disappointed me.  When I found myself needing wood glue again and saw this at half the price and with great reviews, I thought I would give it a try.  I learned the hard way that there is a reason it's so inexpensive.  It simply doesn't hold for very long.  I'm talking days.  The longest hold I was able to get was a couple of weeks, but only because I avoided touching what I had used it on for a majority of that time.  I'm grateful it was only about $5 that I wasted as this will be going in the trash when I finish this. And I just purchased gorilla glue .... which I should have done in the first place.

source_doc: It worked great till it didn't. I have to say I don't have any complaints about this unit, except for the tire inflator. My first one I received wouldn't hold a charge and was sent back. The new one was perfect. I have had it for exactly 2 years. The only problem I ran into is that I have only used the inflator maybe 6 times. I pumped up a basket ball, my sons bike tires a few times, and my two front tires. Unfortunately in putting air into my tires it stopped (main reason for buying). I pumped one tire, let it rest, and started the other one. After about a minute, the compressor was running, but no air was going into the tire. It just stopped, not to sure what happened. This unit is still like brand new, and has been well kept. Everything else still works, and I can use it as an alternate power source. I am not happy that it doesn't inflate anymore, but I can still find uses for it as another power source. So there is that.
